12178503.text: Fritz, the number one seed in Stockholm, beat Norrie to reach the quarterfinals, closing out the match with his 13th ace. Norrie started well, dictating with his forehand, including a forehand winner up the line, and hitting good returns. Fritz grew into the match as his forehand warmed up, stepping in to take it early and serving well out wide. Fritz saved two set points and then took the first set 7-5. He was focused from the start and showed no ill effects from his previous tournament in Paris.

12178671.text: Musetti won 6-1 6-4 in 71 minutes, starting brilliantly and striking the ball cleanly off both forehand and backhand, with several strong volleys. Samuel had already played three matches during the week. He made some solid defensive plays but could not match Musetti, who took the first set and then broke early in the second, helped by a ball that clipped the net and dropped over.

12178945.text: Shevchenko, a qualifier from Kazakhstan, beat defending champion Ruud 6-7, 6-4, 6-3 to reach his first quarterfinal in Stockholm. Ruud won the first set in a tiebreak after a turnaround, sealing it with a shot that came more off the frame than the strings. The balls were said to get rough after six or seven games, which made winners hard to hit. The turning point came in the second set, when Ruud had two break points for a 4-2 lead and could not take them. Shevchenko responded well, seemed to have plenty of time on the ball, hit strong forehands and moved on quickly from setbacks. He came back to take the second set and then the match, finishing with a backhand.

12178957.text: Tabilo, the number four seed from Chile, beat Sonego 7-6 6-7 7-5 in Stockholm to reach the quarterfinal after just under three hours of play in which serve dominated. Sonego had come through qualifying, so he had played extra matches before this one, and his forehand was a strong weapon from the opening game. He often used it to push Tabilo off balance and then came forward to finish points at the net. The match had several close exchanges at the net and a number of drop shots, though at least one drop shot from Tabilo was well short of good enough. Sonego had a match point but missed an overhead, and Tabilo went on to win the deciding set.

12179122.text: Kecmanovic and Rune played the last match of the day in Stockholm, late at night, on the same court where Rune had played 12 months earlier. Rune made many errors from the start and finished the first set with 14 unforced errors, while Kecmanovic hit hard off the forehand and did not have to do much to win the set with a double break. Rune followed one slow first serve to the net and was passed by a Kecmanovic forehand. The match turned after Rune made his first break early in the second set, and from then on he hardly missed a ball, returned very well and used his serve to set up points. Rune completed the comeback to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face the number one seed Fritz.

12179386.text: Tabilo beat Michelsen 7-5 7-6 to reach the semi-final in Stockholm, his first indoor semi-final, a day after a three-set win. Tabilo used the drop shot well and was strong at the net, with good volleys and a well-placed lob that set up a winning overhead. Michelsen broke first in the opening set and saved two break-back points, but Tabilo broke back on his third chance and came from behind to win the set. Michelsen's forehand worked well, finishing several points and producing back-to-back winners, and he also showed good touch on the volley. The second set was tight, and Tabilo got out of trouble on his own serve before winning it, as the slightly better player against a Michelsen who pushed him hard.

12179396.text: Musetti played with strapping under his right knee. Humbert attacked throughout, hitting the ball very hard at times and mixing in a delicate change of pace, while Musetti defended from deep behind the baseline and still found winners, several of them off the backhand. The first set lasted about an hour and the match went to a deciding set in Stockholm. Musetti won to reach the semifinals, with an outstanding lob bringing up match point.

12179510.text: Tirante won to reach his first semi-final in Stockholm and his second of the year, after a hard fight against Shevchenko. Shevchenko had a tight turnaround after a match that ended around quarter past ten the night before. Tirante took the first set in a tiebreak on his fourth set point, having failed to convert four break points earlier in the set, while Shevchenko could not earn a single break point in that period. Tirante hit hard on the forehand and mixed it with drop shots, and his defence often turned into attack. Shevchenko kept fighting with belief even when behind and won the second set, but the match ran over two hours without the best quality. Tirante got the only break of serve in the deciding set and finished the match with an ace.

12179696.text: Alcaraz won the first set 6-2 in 31 minutes in a very one-sided start and he went for his shots from the beginning. His returns did much of the damage, including a strong return off a big second serve from Medvedev and he kept breaking serve while covering the whole court. Medvedev looked lost, shrugging his shoulders and shaking his head as the breaks went against him. Alcaraz briefly lost focus and gave up break chances but he held on. Alcaraz preferred the faster court in Turin to the slower court at Indian Wells, where Medvedev had beaten him. He finished with a one-sided win, looked relaxed throughout and moved to two wins from two matches this week.

12179698.text: Alcaraz made a very fast start in Turin, breaking Tiafoe's serve more than once early in the opening set. He changed direction easily from cross-court to down the line and played with great intelligence, speeding up in the middle of points to win them. Tiafoe had a very hard first six games and lost the first set 6-2. He showed fine touch at times but Alcaraz stayed one step ahead throughout. Alcaraz gave a near perfect display that was strong in every part of his game.

12179699.text: Cobolli made a fast start, breaking Tiafoe's serve to love in the opening game. Tiafoe was close to falling behind 4-1 with a double break in the first set but fought back to level. He then came back from 4-6 down in the tiebreak to take the first set and that comeback proved to be the key to the match. Tiafoe broke early in the second set, kept improving and pulled away, while Cobolli had a tough night. Tiafoe kept his emotions under control in a loud arena in Turin and handled both the occasion and the crowd to win on his debut at the ATP Finals.

12179700.text: Jodar won the first set 6-4 even though his first serve percentage stayed in the low 40s and Fils was angry with himself for letting the set slip after he had been the one with break points. Fils took control in the second set, which was fairly comfortable for him once he broke, while Jodar looked to be struggling physically. Fils kept pressing to the end and hit with pinpoint accuracy, winning 4-6 6-2 6-2. It was his first win at the ATP Finals and it keeps him in contention for the semifinals.

12179701.text: Cobolli made his debut at the event and Medvedev beat him in straight sets. The first set went to a tiebreak after five break points came and went and Medvedev was too solid in the tiebreak. Medvedev played well, especially on serve, where his first serve worked very well. The match was played on a quick indoor hard court, conditions that favoured Medvedev.

12179703.text: Shelton won his first ever match at the ATP Finals in just under two hours. He played a very strong opening set and served well throughout, mixing big serves into the body with wide serves. His backhand was a real weapon, producing several clean winners and he also hit big forehands. Fils pushed hard and won some of the best points of the match and both players reached a high level at times.

12179704.text: Shelton beat Jodar on day five in Turin. The first set went to a tiebreak, which Shelton won 10-8 after he survived a chance for Jodar late in the breaker and his backhand held up well toward the end. Jodar produced some strong returns, including a very deep one off a fast second serve into his forehand that left Shelton little to do. After the tiebreak Shelton held serve well, hitting the ball aggressively to big deep targets and he kept hurting Jodar, at one point leaving him almost on the ground. The win gave Shelton two wins out of three in the group but his place in the semi-finals was not yet guaranteed and depended on the evening match.

12179705.text: Zverev beat Shelton 6-2 7-6 in straight sets to reach the semifinals. Shelton won the toss and opened with big serves but Zverev raised his level and took the first set 6-2 in 38 minutes with a double break, mixing in some slice. Later Shelton came forward more and won points with crisp volleys and the second set went to a tiebreak. The win made Zverev seven out of seven against Shelton and put him in the final four for the fifth time in his career.

12179706.text: Zverev won in straight sets in fast indoor conditions, finishing his group with three wins from three, six sets won out of six and still without losing his serve all week. He had already won the McEnroe group before the match. The match ended in a long tiebreak in which five points in a row were saved before Zverev closed it out. Zverev hit several well-struck passing shots, including a fine backhand and finished points well around the net. Zverev will play either Medvedev or Tiafoe in Saturday's semi-finals and Shelton went through in second place from the group.

12179707.text: Zverev beat Jodar 6-4, 6-4 in just under an hour and a half, in the opening singles match of the week. Jodar, aged 20 and making his debut at the event, came through his first two service games well but his serve was named as an area where he can still improve. The ball was not flying through the air and the players seemed to struggle at times to control it. Zverev served big and posted a high first serve percentage, taking the first set after 40 minutes. The second set followed a similar pattern. Jodar's movement and athleticism were good enough to compete at this level but Zverev's serving proved a little too much for him.

12179750.text: Tirante beat Tabilo 7-5, 7-6 in Stockholm to reach his first tour-level final, at his third attempt. Tirante was dominant on serve early, dropping just one point in his first service games and his net play was excellent as he moved forward at the earliest chance and finished points there. Tabilo showed good touch and used the whole court but at times his shot choices were unclear and some of his volleys were not good enough to win the point. A single break of serve decided the first set. In the second set Tirante had a chance to serve out the match but could not take it because of nerves, then won the tiebreak.

12179838.text: Fritz, the top seed, beat the third seed Musetti 6-4 6-2 in the semi-final in Stockholm. Fritz played with aggression from the start, stepping in to take the ball early. The key break came in the third game and Fritz served very well while keeping Musetti under pressure. His forehand produced many winners and he finished with 24 winners as Musetti had no answer to his attack. His tactics worked throughout and he reached his sixth final of the year and his first in Stockholm.

12179948.text: Fritz won the Stockholm final against Tirante in three sets, taking his first indoor title and the 12th title of his career. Fritz broke early in the first set after some strong defence and played well in that set but Tirante improved and took the second set to force a deciding set. Tirante played aggressive, attacking tennis and came to the net often, winning several points with his volleys, though some volleys were not good enough. Fritz hit some powerful returns and found his forehand more and more often as the match went on and he returned to his first-set level to close it out. Tirante, playing in his first final, pushed Fritz all the way and Fritz's experience may have made the difference.
